# Scene gallery

<!-- Generated by `vidgen gallery`; do not edit. -->

Every vidgen scene type, rendered from its sample in the author guide (`AGENTS.md`,
`vidgen guide scenes`). The previews are animated: each GIF plays the scene at 16:9 and
9:16 and holds its last beat (viewers who ask for reduced motion see that still instead).
Each page has the YAML, the params, the action targets and the stills. The cell-biology and
cartoon sections end with showcases, small scenes written for the gallery, each a whole `video.yaml`.
Regenerate with `vidgen gallery`.

## Genetics

A whole medical-genetics video, one inherited disease from a family's pedigree to the variant, a carrier test and the population: [Cystic fibrosis: from a family to a diagnosis](../../examples/cystic-fibrosis/README.md) (`examples/cystic-fibrosis`). Notation, exact numbers and counselling tone: [the genetics cookbook](../COOKBOOK-GENETICS.md).

## Science charts

A whole physics explainer with plots and calculations, simulated nuclei, counts with a fit, the half-life worked out and carbon-14 dating: [Half-life: how radioactive decay keeps time](../../examples/radioactive-decay/README.md) (`examples/radioactive-decay`). Honest axes, error bars, fits, units and significant figures: [the science-charts cookbook](../COOKBOOK-SCIENCE-CHARTS.md).

| type | preview | use it for |

## Orbital mechanics

A whole orbital-mechanics explainer, why a rocket cannot fly straight to Mars, the Hohmann transfer, the transfer time and the departure burn worked out, the planets on a real date: [How to get to Mars](../../examples/mars-transfer/README.md) (`examples/mars-transfer`). Scale honesty, units, approximations to state and pacing: [the orbits cookbook](../COOKBOOK-ORBITS.md).

| type or showcase | preview | use it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`orbit`](orbit.md) | <a href="orbit.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/orbit-16x9.png"><img src="media/orbit-16x9.gif" height="180" alt="orbit at 16:9"></picture></a> <a href="orbit.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/orbit-9x16.png"><img src="media/orbit-9x16.gif" height="180" alt="orbit at 9:16"></picture></a> | planets, moons, satellites or a comet on their orbits, moving in correct timing (Kepler's laws, the inner planets for a year, the ISS and a geostationary orbit, a flyby); mutual gravity; manoeuvres: burns, Hohmann / bi-elliptic / phasing transfers with their Δv, phase angle and launch windows, a gravity assist; many bodies: Lagrange points and Trojans in the rotating frame, the figure-eight, binary stars, the Io–Europa–Ganymede resonance, tides (a schematic); the Solar System on a date (1800–2050), the next opposition or conjunction, all planets on a log scale, an inset of the inner planets, planet sizes to scale |
| [The Hohmann transfer to Mars](mars_hohmann.md) | <a href="mars_hohmann.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/mars_hohmann-16x9.png"><img src="media/mars_hohmann-16x9.gif" height="180" alt="mars_hohmann at 16:9"></picture></a> <a href="mars_hohmann.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/mars_hohmann-9x16.png"><img src="media/mars_hohmann-9x16.gif" height="180" alt="mars_hohmann at 9:16"></picture></a> | a transfer between two planets: the phase angle at the launch window, two burns on words, the Δv and the time computed |
| [Trojans in the rotating frame](jupiter_trojans.md) | <a href="jupiter_trojans.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/jupiter_trojans-16x9.png"><img src="media/jupiter_trojans-16x9.gif" height="180" alt="jupiter_trojans at 16:9"></picture></a> <a href="jupiter_trojans.md"><picture><source media="(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)" srcset="media/jupiter_trojans-9x16.png"><img src="media/jupiter_trojans-9x16.gif" height="180" alt="jupiter_trojans at 9:16"></picture></a> | a three-body system in the frame turning with Jupiter: the five Lagrange points standing still, a Trojan's tadpole inside its zero-velocity curve |
